messages:
Olga (support): FYI — customer ACME filed an escalation after a pen test disclosure. They're seeing a big billing delta and occasional 502s on audit export calls. Ticket: #8342.

PenTestBot: automated submission from external-redteam: ID ptest-2026-03-12-77. Attachments: repro log + curl steps.

Elaine (sec): Can you paste the redteam repro here? I want to confirm scope before we touch infra.

Olga (support): From the tester: 
```
# hit export endpoint with parallel sessions and signed session cookie
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/admin/audit/export -d '{"range":"last_30d","format":"ndjson"}' &
done
```
They said sometimes the endpoint returns an exported file with keys for unrelated projects (other customers) and that the response time spiked to >30s.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Whoa — unrelated project data is a big one. That suggests a keying or tenant isolation bug in the export path, or an upstream cache miss returning the wrong blob. Any log snippets?

Olga (support): Tester included this snippet from the exporter service log: 
```
[2026-03-12T18:22:03Z] export: start tenant=acme, job=job-87
[2026-03-12T18:22:05Z] storage: fetched object key=export-cache/2026-03-12/job-87-blob, matched-tenant=acme
[2026-03-12T18:22:06Z] export: stream open, reading 1.2GB
[2026-03-12T18:22:06Z] export: verified-hsm-attestation=true, kms-key=projects/global/keys/redwood-audit
[2026-03-12T18:22:36Z] export: stream end, served-blob-tenant=beta-corp
```
Note the last line — served-blob-tenant mismatch.

Elaine (sec): That log looks like the blob metadata claimed acme but the stored object was for beta-corp. Could be a race in the caching/garbage-collection or a stale mapping in our object metadata index. Also worried about HSM/KMS attest logs showing up — need to check decrypt audit trail.

Kai (infra-sre): On it. I can query object metadata and cloud audit trail for that job id. Suggest we freeze further exports for ACME until we confirm. We should also toggle a short-lived feature-flag to force fresh read-through (bypass cache) while we triage.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Quick repro suggestion for the team: run the export with a unique marker in the payload and do a parallel run for a different tenant to try to force collision. Example: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME" -X POST ... -d '{"note":"ptest-marker-a1"}' &
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $BETA" -X POST ... -d '{"note":"ptest-marker-b1"}' &
```
If beta marker appears in acme blob, we have cross-tenant contamination.

Harold (product): Severity question from legal: if the exported file contained other customer PII, we need to treat as confirmed data-exposure and notify affected customers and regulators. Elaine, what's your take on severity?

Elaine (sec): Tentative severity: high (data exposure between tenants). But we need to confirm three things: 1) actual PII present, 2) production-retention policy was bypassed, 3) if the key separation (KMS per-tenant) was respected. If HSM attestation was reused incorrectly and allowed label leakage, that raises severity to critical.

PenTestBot: tester followed up in-thread: "I reproduced 3x. Export sometimes resolved to blob ids from the global export-cache. Attacker with ability to replay session cookies could mass-export. I did NOT test retention deletion or KMS key extraction."

Kai (infra-sre): I pulled a quick mapping for job-87. S3 object metadata shows owner=beta-corp for the underlying object id, but the index entry pointed to job-87 -> object-id-442. There's a race window where object-id reuse can happen during GC when object keys are recycled. GC logs show a concurrent cleanup at 18:22:04 for object-id-440..443.

Jamal (eng-runtime): That matches a bug class we fixed in a staging refactor — index writes not properly atomic with object creation. Hypothesis: exporter writes index entry, GC recycles old object id, new export references recycled object id before metadata updated.

Olga (support): Customer impacted: ACME (account id acme-101). They reported 220GB exported and billing spiked ~$1,200 in one hour because of repeated retries. They're requesting mitigation and reimbursement.

Elaine (sec): Immediate action items:
- Kai: disable export-cache recycling and flip to never-reuse IDs (hotfix).
- Jamal: add a read-through bypass flag and an assertion that object-id owner == requested-tenant in exporter.
- Support/Olga: draft customer communication template (no admission of root cause yet) — say we're investigating possible export inconsistencies and will pause exports.
- Harold: prepare legal/regulator brief if we confirm cross-tenant PII.

Kai (infra-sre): Pushing hotfix to staging now (no downtime, toggled via FF). I'll also pull KMS cryptographic logs: queries for decrypt attempts at 2026-03-12T18:20-18:30Z for key redwood-audit.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Also add a detection rule for anomalous export rate per API key (e.g., >50 exports/hour) and throttle. That would have blocked the high-volume replay.

Elaine (sec): One more check: did the tester use presigned URLs or session cookies? Presigned URLs can bypass some of our tenant-binding checks if improperly signed. PenTestBot — can you confirm?

PenTestBot: tester: "I used regular session tokens only; I replayed cookies and accelerated concurrency. No presigned URLs."

Elaine (sec): OK. That indicates session-replay + index race is likely root cause. Next steps: reproduce end-to-end in a clean env, confirm whether KMS/HSM per-tenant keys were used (or global audit key) and whether HSM attestation was re-used. Kai, can you attach the raw cloudtrail and hsm-attest lines here when ready?

Kai (infra-sre): Will do. Quick preview of HSM lines: 
```
2026-03-12T18:22:06Z hsm: attest session=att-9932 tenant=redwood-global action=attest ok=true nonce=0x9af...
2026-03-12T18:22:06Z hsm: key-use key=redwood-audit usage=decrypt caller=exporter-2
```
I'm pulling more.

Harold (product): For the customer note: propose we pause exports for affected accounts, refund export-ingestion charges for the window, and offer a dedicated consult to verify no PII left in other exports. Legal will advise on regulator timelines.

Olga (support): I'll draft a message and queue it for Elaine review.

Elaine (sec): Final ask before triage call: Jamal and Kai, please produce a short repro run in a staging tenant with the parallel curl pattern and upload the exported ndjson to the secure evidence bucket. Add a checksum and signed timestamp. We'll use that for severity and to validate the fix once hotfix lands.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Copy. I'll run it now with markers and attach results within 2 hours.

Kai (infra-sre): Hotfix toggled in prod to disable ID recycling. Monitoring on export errors and cross-tenant indicators turned on. Updating last_message_ts.

Elaine (sec): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after Jamal's repro and Kai's HSM/trail artifacts.
